title: Event-Driven Application Patterns
description: Use common event-driven patterns to build scalable and maintainable cloud applications.

data.text: Event-driven architecture has proven patterns that solve recurring problems. Understanding these patterns helps you design systems that are easy to extend, test, and scale.

terms.definition: Store all state changes as events. Rebuild state by replaying the event log.
Command Query Responsibility Segregation -- separate models for writing and reading data.
Coordinate distributed transactions across services using a series of local transactions and compensating actions.
Save events to a database in the same transaction as the business operation, then publish them asynchronously.

data.text: The outbox pattern solves a common problem: how do you save data to a database and publish an event reliably in the same operation? You write the event to an outbox table in the same database transaction as your business data. A background process reads the outbox and publishes events to Azure Service Bus or Event Grid.

data.caption: The Outbox pattern for reliable event publishing
data.definition:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Application
    participant DB as Database
    participant Worker as Outbox Worker
    participant Bus as Service Bus
    App->>DB: BEGIN TRANSACTION
    App->>DB: INSERT order
    App->>DB: INSERT outbox (event)
    App->>DB: COMMIT
    loop Every 5 seconds
      Worker->>DB: SELECT unpublished events
      Worker->>Bus: Publish event
      Worker->>DB: Mark as published
    end

data.text: A saga is a sequence of local transactions across services. If a transaction fails, the saga runs compensating transactions to undo previous steps. This avoids distributed transactions, which are hard to scale.

data.title: Start Simple
data.text: You do not need all patterns at once. Start with Service Bus queues for basic messaging, add topics for fan-out, and adopt more advanced patterns like outbox and saga only when your use case demands them.

data.title: Design an Event-Driven Order System
data.description: Design a simple event-driven system for processing orders using the patterns you learned.
steps: Use the outbox pattern to publish an OrderCreated event.
Use a saga to coordinate inventory reservation, payment, and shipping.
Use Event Grid to notify downstream services when an order is shipped.
data.expectedOutcome: A design document describing how the three patterns work together.
